faqs.a:
The city owns and operates a public water system that supplies safe drinking water
               to citizens. As the operator of a public water system, the city is required to comply
               with Colorado State regulations that protect city drinking water from potential contamination
               from an uncontrolled cross-connection. The City Council has determined that an uncontrolled
               cross-connection presents a risk to the integrity of the public water system and to
               the health and safety of the public. It is the intent of the City Council to protect
               the city's water system from contamination due to backflow from a private water system,
               and to provide for the maintenance of a continuing cross-connection control program
               to help prevent the contamination of the city's water system. The purpose of this
               article is to comply with Colorado health and safety laws and regulations that require
               the city to protect its public water system from contaminants or pollutants that could
               enter the distribution system by backflow from a customer's water supply system through
               the service connection.
(
Ord. No. 4829
, § 1, 12-5-2022)
